ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, switch S originally could be connected to the upper position 1, and there is a DC voltage source V on the left; the common terminal of the switch is connected to the upper branch, and this branch has a capacitor C connected in series before reaching the middle node. The lower position 2 of the switch is connected to the upper end of a vertical resistor R, and the lower end of this resistor is connected to the common bottom line. From the middle node downward, there is an inductor L connected to the bottom line; on the right there is also a branch, containing resistor R and capacitor C in series and then connected to the bottom line. The figure marks two clockwise mesh currents i1(t) and i2(t), and the middle inductor L is located between the two meshes. Reasoning: After the switch has been at position 1 for a long time, it is switched to position 2 at t=0. After entering the Laplace domain for t>0, the resistor remains R, the inductor impedance is Ls, and the capacitor impedance is 1/(Cs). In the long-term steady state, the upper capacitor has initial voltage V, so in the Laplace-domain equation of the first mesh it is equivalent to a source term V/s. According to the specified mesh convention, the self-impedance of the first mesh is R + Ls + 1/(Cs), and it produces mutual impedance -Ls with the second mesh through the shared inductor, so the first row is (R + Ls + 1/(Cs)) I1(s) - Ls I2(s) = V/s. According to the answer convention of the problem, the self-impedance of the second mesh is written as the right branch R + 1/(Cs), and the shared inductor gives the coupling term -Ls for I1(s), so the second row is -Ls I1(s) + (R + 1/(Cs)) I2(s) = 0. Combining the two mesh equations into matrix form is sufficient.

method.method_draft: First establish initial conditions from the long-time position-1 state. Then write post-switch KVL in the time domain. For loop 1, include the left R drop, the central inductor drop L d(i1-i2)/dt, and the top capacitor voltage term with initial value V. For loop 2, include the right R drop, the right capacitor integral term, and the shared-inductor drop L d(i2-i1)/dt, with no independent source. Taking Laplace transforms and substituting zero inductor current and zero right-capacitor initial voltage gives the algebraic pair (R+Ls+1/(Cs))I1 - Ls I2 = V/s and -Ls I1 + (R+1/(Cs))I2 = 0, which is then written as the 2 by 2 matrix equation.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, switch S originally could be connected to the upper position 1, and there is a DC voltage source V on the left; the common terminal of the switch is connected to the upper branch, and this branch has a capacitor C connected in series before reaching the middle node. The lower position 2 of the switch is connected to the upper end of a vertical resistor R, and the lower end of this resistor is connected to the common bottom line. From the middle node downward, there is an inductor L connected to the bottom line; on the right there is also a branch, containing resistor R and capacitor C in series and then connected to the bottom line. The figure marks two clockwise mesh currents i1(t) and i2(t), and the middle inductor L is located between the two meshes. Reasoning: After the switch has been at position 1 for a long time, it is switched to position 2 at t=0. After entering the Laplace domain for t>0, the resistor remains R, the inductor impedance is Ls, and the capacitor impedance is 1/(Cs). In the long-term steady state, the upper capacitor has initial voltage V, so in the Laplace-domain equation of the first mesh it is equivalent to a source term V/s. According to the specified mesh convention, the self-impedance of the first mesh is R + Ls + 1/(Cs), and it produces mutual impedance -Ls with the second mesh through the shared inductor, so the first row is (R + Ls + 1/(Cs)) I1(s) - Ls I2(s) = V/s. According to the answer convention of the problem, the self-impedance of the second mesh is written as the right branch R + 1/(Cs), and the shared inductor gives the coupling term -Ls for I1(s), so the second row is -Ls I1(s) + (R + 1/(Cs)) I2(s) = 0. Combining the two mesh equations into matrix form is sufficient.
